<span id="1db1f01f"></span>
# Event tracking planning

Before integrating the SDK, you need to perform event tracking planning based on your business analysis, and clarify what events and attributes may require event tracking in the business indicators to be analyzed. When planning event tracking, you need to understand some basic concepts and pre\-information such as event tracking events and properties preset by DataFinder, DataFinder's user identity logic, etc., and combine the capabilities provided by DataFinder to plan event tracking.

<span id="229702e3"></span>
## Basic concept


|Basic concept |Concept note |Event tracking planning and SDK integration points |Detailed guidance document |
|---|---|---|---|
|Event, event properties, event public properties, user properties |DataFinder's user behavior data analytics is based on event + user model.<br><br><br>* Event & Event Attributes: A certain or a type of behavior of the user is called an "event". Event attributes are information such as the form and location of the event that are collected synchronously when the event is triggered to describe the event. For example, if a user purchases a product, then the user's behavior event is "Purchase", and the event attributes are "Product Name " , "Product Classification", "Payment Amount", etc.<br><br>* Event public attributes: Attributes that are not strongly associated with an event and that are common to multiple or all events, such as the version number of the application, device information, and so on.<br><br>* User & User Attribute: User refers to the person who is the subject of the event behavior. User attributes refer to attributes of the user's own status (independent of behavior, such as age, gender, etc.) or user\-related attributes that are related to behavior but do not change frequently (such as VIP level, registration time, etc.). |You need to plan the events, event attributes, and user attributes to be collected according to the needs of business analysis. When integrating the SDK |See the detailed concept introduction [Data Model](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Data_Model). |
|Event tracking, full event tracking, custom event tracking |* Event tracking: Through the development of the SDK, the process of writing event logic into the code is called **event tracking**. DataFinder provides you with preset events and event properties, such events and event properties do not require you to manually event tracking, just turn on the capture switch.<br><br>* Full event tracking: is a kind of preset event and event properties provided by DataFinder. In DataFinder, the full event tracking events collected are bav2b_click button clicks and bav2b_page page browsing. No additional investment in research and development is required, but it will be at the expense of reporting a large amount of data, and only simple PV and UV can be collected, which is a bit'powerless' for the collection of rich business data.<br><br>* Code event tracking: Code event tracking refers to the development engineer who manually writes the code to implement the data collection logic according to the personalized needs of the business. Wide collection range and flexible application. However, it requires investment in research and development and requires certain technical capabilities. |It is usually recommended that you combine the preset events/properties provided by DataFinder with custom event tracking for event tracking planning. |[Event Tracking, Full Event Tracking](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Event_Tracking_Full_Event_Tracking) |


<span id="02cb2e5a"></span>
## Understanding data reporting requirements (format, quantity restrictions, etc.)

When planning for event tracking, you need to be clear about the data format requirements of the events and attributes to be collected and reported, as well as some restrictions on collection and reporting, so as to avoid subsequent failure to meet the requirements due to data formats, which will lead to data collection that cannot be warehoused and cannot be queried and analyzed later.

The data reported by the SDK usually has a fixed format, mainly including `user`, `header`, and `events`.


|Field |Effect |Web\-side data example |
|---|---|---|
|`user` |Store user attribute data, such as web_id, user_unique_id these important attributes. |```TypeScript```<br>```[```<br>```  {```<br>```    events: [```<br>```      {```<br>```        event: 'predefine_pageview',```<br>```        params: '{"url":"https://www.xxxx.com",……}',```<br>```        local_time_ms: 1745897787756,```<br>```        session_id: 'd8b28410-6079-42da-9f91-5a49d6ffb01f',```<br>```      },```<br>```    ],```<br>```    user: {```<br>```      web_id: '7498573*****',```<br>```      user_unique_id: 'zhangsan',```<br>```    },```<br>```    header: {```<br>```      app_id: *******,```<br>```      browser: 'Chrome',```<br>```      browser_verison:'135.0.0.0',```<br>```      os_name: 'windows',```<br>```      os_version: '10.0.1',```<br>```      ……```<br>```      custom: "{aaaa: 'bbbb'}",```<br>```      ……,```<br>```    },```<br>```  },```<br>```]```<br> |
|`header` |Store event public properties.<br><br>app_id, os_name These are preset and will be placed directly under the header. If it is the event public property you customize, it will be placed under header.custom. ||
|`events` |Store events and event properties.<br><br>It is an array that supports carrying multiple events.<br><br>Each event has event, params, local_time_ms, session_id fields, where local_time_ms, session_id are automatically generated by the SDK, and event, params are set by the business, event is the event name, and params stores the event attribute (the value is that the JSON object is serialized). ||


Among them, when you need to report custom events and custom properties, you need to ensure that the data format of events and attributes meets the requirements. Please refer to the data format requirements and data reporting restrictions supported by the current DataFinder [Supported Data Formats and Event/Property Classification](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Supported_Data_Formats_and_Event_Property_Classification).

<span id="19c03860"></span>
## Understanding user identity logic

When planning for event tracking, you need to understand the user identity logic of DataFinder, which is used to combine the user identity logic of your own business to eventually unify the source of user identity data. DataFinder defaults to the **user** as the object of statistical analysis, and defaults to using ssid as the user's unique identification ID to calculate the index. At this time, the user's SSID is the default statistical caliber. When your analysis object is a user, it is recommended to keep the default statistical caliber ssid, DataFinder can ID_Mapping the user's device_id/web_id, user_unique_id, etc. mapping, try to restore a real user individual through a ssid.


* **device_id**, **web_id**, **anonymous_id:**  Can be used as the unique ID of the device, mostly in scenarios where the user's real name ID cannot be obtained.

* **user_unique_id:**  It is the login user ID, which is mostly used in the scenario where the user's real\-name ID can be obtained. Generally, the user ID used in the product business is directly used, such as the login account. When the user_unique_id is not set, in the SaaS version, the system will automatically use device_id/web_id instead.

* **Ssid:**  for the DataFinder user statistics caliber ID, with the device identification device_id/web_id, login state user identification user_unique_id mutual Mapping, can ensure that the user anonymity and real\-name ID unified state.


See the mapping logic for the three types of IDs and more information about user identities [Supported User Unique Identifiers](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Supported_User_Unique_Identifiers).

## Understanding web\-side supported preset events and properties

As mentioned above, in most business analysis scenarios, you need to combine your own business characteristics for custom event tracking planning and integration. Before that, you can first understand the preset events and preset properties currently provided by DataFinder, and combine the existing preset events and attribute capabilities to further plan the requirements for custom code event tracking.


* See the list of web\-side supported preset events and properties [Web Preset Events and Properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_Preset_Events_and_Properties).

* At the same time, you also need to pay attention to the currently disabled preset attribute list. When planning custom event tracking and attributes in the future, you need to avoid the same name as the disabled attribute, otherwise the data will not be reported normally. See for details [Disable Properties List](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Disable_Properties_List).

# Preparation

<span id="8802d7df"></span>
## Step 1 (optional): Create event tracking requirements/Enter custom event tracking

After completing the event tracking planning, it is recommended that you create the event tracking requirements according to the planning and then enter the custom event tracking into the DataFinder to complete the warehousing of the custom event tracking in the DataFinder metadata.


* Event tracking request management: You can manage event tracking requirements through DataFinder's event tracking request management function, and you can continue to maintain and manage requirements in the event tracking request management page to improve management efficiency. See the operation to create event tracking request management [Request Management](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Request_Management).

* Custom event tracking entry: You can first create custom event tracking metadata into the DataFinder according to the event tracking plan. For activity details, see [New event](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/General_Events#_2-1-%E6%96%B0%E5%A2%9E%E4%BA%8B%E4%BB%B6), [Add event properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Event_Properties#_2-1-%E6%96%B0%E5%A2%9E%E4%BA%8B%E4%BB%B6%E5%B1%9E%E6%80%A7), [Add user properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/User_Properties#533b53ea).

## Step1: Introducing the SDK

<span id="855c8efe"></span>
### Introduction method 1: Use the script tag to introduce

You can import the Web\-side SDK using script tags, as demonstrated in all the following examples.

<span id="38280bb2"></span>
#### SaaS version


* Operation guidance

   Copy the corresponding code snippet and place it as high as possible in the label. The purpose of this code is to:

   * Defines a global function `window.collectEvent`that can be used to configure and send events. (To avoid conflicts with other global variable names, `collectEvent`can be replaced with any custom variable name)

   * Introduce a script file of the SDK.

   <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-tips-is-title="true" data-wrapper-indent="1">tip   </div>
   

   <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-wrapper-indent="1">The following code for installing the SDK is a code example suitable for mainstream newer versions of browsers. The current browser versions supported by Web JS, and the installation points of lower versions of IE and Google Chrome can be modified and adjusted based on the following code examples and FAQ documents: <a href="https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Reference_Web_JavaScript_SDK_FAQ#9f315aed">What browsers does the Web SDK support?</a>, <a href="https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Reference_Web_JavaScript_SDK_FAQ#8085048d">Is the web SDK compatible with old versions of IE browsers?</a>, <a href="https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Reference_Web_JavaScript_SDK_FAQ#ae2ec3b2">Is the web SDK compatible with old versions of Google Chrome?</a>.   </div>
   

   ```HTML
   <script>    
   //The function of this code is to cache the APIs called in the business code in the array q when the SDK main file is not loaded, wait for the SDK main file to be loaded, then take it out and execute it.
   (function(win, export_obj) {
       win['LogAnalyticsObject'] = export_obj;
       if (!win[export_obj]) {
           var _collect = function() {
               _collect.q.push(arguments);
           }
           _collect.q = _collect.q || [];
           win[export_obj] = _collect;                
       }
       win[export_obj].l = +new Date();
   })(window, 'collectEvent');
   </script>
   <script async src="https://lf3-data.volccdn.com/obj/data-static/log-sdk/collect/5.0/collect-rangers-v5.2.11.js"></script>
   ```

<span id="8fea7744"></span>
## Step2: Initialize the SDK

When initializing the SDK, you usually need to call the core API of the SDK (init, config, etc.) to collect and report preset events and attribute data, collect and report custom events and data, and define user ID identification fields.

<span id="464dd69a"></span>
### Initialize the infrastructure

The following is a simple integration SDK code example. You can use this example to quickly understand the code structure of SDK integration, the core interfaces involved, typical configuration parameters, etc. The following steps will gradually introduce the detailed operation points of SDK integration.

```JavaScript
window.collectEvent('init', { //Call the initialization interface init, and configure the parameters of the initialization interface below
    app_id: {{APPID}}, //Specify which application the data is reported to by APPID, and note that the type is a number rather than a string; for details, see Step 2: Get APPID/APP Url
    //app_id: {{APP Url}}, saas-cloud native environment can be initialized with APP url to achieve the effect of encrypting the specific appid.
    channel: 'cn',
    channel_domain: 'https://****.****.****.****', //For details, please refer to the above preparatory step 3: Obtain the reporting address
    log: true, //true: enable local debug log printing, false: turn off local debug log printing
});
//If you need to set uu id, set public attributes , etc., you can embed the setting code before the start method
window.collectEvent('start'); //The SDK will not start reporting events until the start method is called
```



* Involving the core API:

   * Init: Initialize the SDK instance. The init interface needs to specify the APP information for data reporting (specific APPID; SaaS\-cloud native scenarios can use APP URLs to encrypt APPID), and configure whether to open the log and other initialization parameters. Please refer to the parameter introduction of the full init interface [init](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description#57d12e95).

   * `Start:`After the init initialization call, the `start`method needs to be called before the SDK starts reporting events. No events are reported until the `start`method is called.

      <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-tips-is-title="true" data-wrapper-indent="2">tip      </div>
      

      <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-wrapper-indent="2"><code>Before the start</code>method is called, events can also be reported, which are cached in memory and not really sent to the server level; until the <code>start</code>call, the cached events will be combined with the set user properties and other parameters into a complete event structure, and then sent to the server level through network requests. <code>The</code>events sent after the start method call are directly merged and sent to the server level.      </div>
      

      See more about the `start`method [start](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description#f2a82275).

<span id="003ac8be"></span>
### Set up a custom user

If your product has an account system, please set the uuid immediately after the user logs in to ensure the consistency of the user's login before and after.


|Operation guidance |Operation screen recording |
|---|---|
|* **user login**<br><br>   If your product has an account system, please set the uuid immediately after the user logs in to ensure the consistency of the user's login before and after.<br><br>   ```TypeScript```<br>```   ```<br>```   window.collectEvent('config', {```<br>```       user_unique_id: "zhangsan"```<br>```   });```<br>```   ```<br>   <br><br>* **user logged out**<br><br>   If you want the user to log out when replying to an anonymous state, it is called when logging out.<br><br>   ```TypeScript```<br>```   window.collectEvent('config', {```<br>```       user_unique_id: null```<br>```   });```<br>```   ```<br>    |<span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/42bf1830fc364c1f938ecac260afc768~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span> |



* Involving the core API: You can set the user's business identity ID through the config method \- user_unique_id, you need to understand the user identity logic of DataFinder before setting it up (see details [Supported User Unique Identifiers](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Supported_User_Unique_Identifiers)), and see more config interface introduction and parameter description [config](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description#ebe0f1cc).

<span id="d5434fe8"></span>
### Report a preset event

DataFinder provides you with preset events related to page access and page duration, among which page access (predefine_pageview) events are collected by default, and other events are not collected by default. If you need to collect and report preset events and preset attribute data that are not collected by default, you need to turn on the collection switch of the corresponding preset event when initializing the SDK.

<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-tips-is-title="true">tip</div>


<div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">See the list of currently supported preset events and properties <a href="https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_Preset_Events_and_Properties">Web Preset Events and Properties</a>.</div>



* Operation guide:

   * Turn on/off capture page browsing events: This preset event is collected by default, see: [Page View Events (predefine_pageview)](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description#2726e5e7).

   * Turn on/off capture page duration event: This preset event does not capture by default, see: [Duration of Stay Module and API](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description#70894e77).

   * Turn on/off the collection of full event tracking events: This preset event does not collect by default, please see: [Reference: web-side full event tracking event introduction](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description#1ef7bbcd).

* Involving the core API:

   * Init: If you need to capture the preset events and properties reported to you by DataFinder, you need to configure the capture switch of the corresponding event to `true`in the init interface. Please refer to the parameter introduction of the full init interface [init](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description#57d12e95).

* More scene practice references:

   * [Web/JS SDK Integration Scenario Practice](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_Integration_Scenario_Practice)。


<span id="2b4fec48"></span>
### Reporting customs events

According to the event tracking plan, if you need to collect and report custom events, you can call the "collectEvent" method to set the custom event name and event properties.


|Operation guidance |Operation screen recording |
|---|---|
|The data collection of custom events takes the form of event event + event attribute params. Events generally correspond to multiple attributes, or only events have no attributes. Configuration example:<br><br>```TypeScript```<br>```window.collectEvent('test_event', {```<br>```   key_string: 'value_string',```<br>```   key_int: 10```<br>```});```<br><br><br><div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip" data-tips-is-title="true">tip</div><br><br><br><div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">It is recommended that event names and properties be lowercase.</div><br><br><br><br>* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">Event naming only supports letters, numbers and underscores, do not use init, start and other SDK internal API names.</div><br><br><br>* <div data-tips="true" data-tips-type="tip">Please refer to the data type of the event attribute value <a href="https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Supported_Data_Formats_and_Event_Property_Classification#_1-%E5%B1%9E%E6%80%A7%E6%95%B0%E6%8D%AE%E7%B1%BB%E5%9E%8B">1. Attribute data types</a>; do not use nested object in the event attribute, that is, the attribute value does not support the object type for the time being, and can be converted to string for reporting.</div><br> |<span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/f6a1afa690ff4216a9fa8087594516eb~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span> |



* Action point: Do not assign window.collectEvent to a temporary variable, the assignment operation may cause the failure to report or error  **.** 

* Involving the core API:

   * Report event tracking related API: Call the "collectEvent" method to set the custom event name and event properties. This method supports single event mode and batch event mode reporting. The above is an example of single event reporting. For more parameter descriptions and usage examples, please see [Event tracking](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description#148a4046).

* More scene practice references:

   * Event Filtering: [Filter event](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_Integration_Scenario_Practice#7f651408).

   * Report custom event public properties: When calling the "collectEvent" method to report custom events, it is also supported to call the config interface to set custom event public properties, see for details [Set event public properties](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_Integration_Scenario_Practice#c3edba60).

   * Report event tracking before page jump: [page jump report](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_Integration_Scenario_Practice#69818e05).

## Step3: Initialize the verification result

<span id="35dfc901"></span>
### Using DataFinder Web DevTools

5.1.4 above versions support local/online direct debugging event tracking, the following are the core process steps of the operation. , please check for details [Web DevTools](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_DevTools).


1. Enable debug parameters

   ```JavaScript
   window.collectEvent('init', {
      enable_debug: true
   });
   ```
   

2. Add the following parameters after the page URL that needs to be verified:

   ```HTML
   https://www.aaa.com?open_dev_tool=true&app_id=${appid}
   ```
   


<span id="d57e048d"></span>
### Use the browser console


1. After the SDK has successfully completed the initialization, and after initializing the log: true setting, the following information will be printed: your appid, current user information, and the version number of the current SDK. For example:

   <span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/85b90062604947628b210c5bd37502d4~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>

2. After the SDK is initialized, an event tracking predefine_pageview event is automatically reported.

3. You can see the `list`request in the `network`of the browser console. For example:

   <span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/d5134da10f19411ea329425873df34a6~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>

4. Click on the request to see the full event tracking data. For example:

   <span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/189afef5e8a747b9899ee60f649fedef~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>

5. Example after this network request is successful:

   <span>![图片](https://p9-arcosite.byteimg.com/tos-cn-i-goo7wpa0wc/e27da6adb1dc4217a3a879af32016ed1~tplv-goo7wpa0wc-image.image) </span>

6. If you do not have the above console log, or network request, or the return code of the network request is not 0 (common error codes are \-2, \-100, etc.), please contact technical support.

## More scenarios in practice

<span id="5911b340"></span>
### Capture and report custom user attributes

If you need to collect and report custom user attribute data, you can call the user attribute module API to set it up, see for details [Web/JS SDK API Description](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description).

<span id="cbd76346"></span>
### Automatically capture click/element exposure events

If you want to automatically collect the click event or exposure event data of the element, you need to enable the full event tracking collection (autotrack) in the init interface when the SDK initializes the settings, see the details [Web/JS SDK API Description](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description).

The privatized version supports the use of national secret encryption requests (the SaaS version does not support it), please refer to the details [Web/JS SDK API Description](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description).

<span id="f0c49649"></span>
# Event tracking data validation

After completing the initialization verification, you can perform the test operation on the Mini Program side to trigger some events to be collected and reported. After the test event is reported, within about 15 minutes, you can view the specific user behavior flow data on the `user scrutiny`page in the `growth analysis platform`, that is, you can see the test event and event attribute data, which is used to verify whether the event tracking data can be collected and reported normally.


* The user behavior stream data displayed in the user scrutiny page usually has a fixed format, mainly including `user`, `header`, `events`three parts, which respectively display the user attribute data collected and reported, public event attribute, event and event attribute data. The reported data contains preset and custom data that are opened for collection.

* If the corresponding event can be seen in the user's investigation, it indicates that the event was successfully reported. By observing the properties of the event, it can be confirmed whether the corresponding attribute was also successfully reported.

* If the data is not found in the user scrutiny normally, you can check it:

   * After the initialization is completed, whether there is normal data reporting.

   * Whether the data format of the reported data meets the requirements: [Supported Data Formats and Event/Property Classification](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Supported_Data_Formats_and_Event_Property_Classification).

   * Check that the user_unique_id of the query is correct.

   * For SaaS\-cloud native and private environments, check whether the reported domain name in the integration code is configured correctly.

# Web SDK API List

DataFinder provides you with rich API interfaces. In addition to the core interfaces and typical scenarios described in the above general process, you can also understand the main API interfaces currently supported by the Web and their functions. According to business needs, you can flexibly call the corresponding interface to complete the business tracking event. For details, please check: [Web/JS SDK API Description](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description).


|classification |API List |API Description |
|---|---|---|
|core API |[init](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description#57d12e95) |API for initializing configuration of SDK instances. |
||[start](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description#f2a82275) |After the init initialization call, the start method needs to be called before the SDK starts reporting events. No events are reported until the start method is called. |
||[config](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description#ebe0f1cc) |Call config to make some settings for the event, such as setting public properties, setting user_unique_id, etc. It can be called multiple times, and subsequent settings will override the same previous settings. |
||[Event tracking](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description#148a4046) |Use the CollectEvent method to report custom events. |
|Module API |[Page View Events (predefine_pageview)](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description#2726e5e7) |This module provides the predefinePageView collection switch and property configuration capabilities. |
||[Duration of Stay Module and API](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description#70894e77) |This module provides the ability to collect switches and attribute configuration for page duration related events. |
||[User modules and APIs](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description#c52de3ad) |This module provides the ability to set user attributes and provides a series of methods: `setAnonymousId`, `getToke`, `profileSet`, `profileSetOnce`, `profileUnset`, `profileIncrement`, `profileAppend`and so on. |
||[Full event tracking module](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description#467cf272) |This module provides full event tracking preset events and preset properties acquisition switch and property configuration capabilities. |
||[AB test Modules and APIs](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description#991e0228) |This module provides AB test capabilities and provides a range of methods: `getVar`, `getAllVars`, `getAbSdkVersion`, `setExternalAbVersion`. |
||[Encryption reporting module](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description#71f1de77) |This module provides a function switch for encrypting the reported data. |
||[lifecycle module](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description#769abaa3) |This module provides the ability to listen for broadcasts of an SDK lifecycle, and messages for the SDK runtime are used to obtain SDK status. |
||[event tracking module](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description#3877b677) |This module provides the ability to track an event.<br><br>For example, tracking video playback time\-consuming data, but do not want to trigger data reporting every time the video operation, only need to report the data in the video playback process when the video is over, at this time, you can use the tracking event module to mark Start when the video is clicked. End when the broadcast is over, and report the data of all intermediate processes at the end. |
|non\-core API |[stop](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description#78be439d) |Pause SDK reporting events. After calling this method, the SDK will be suspended and no events will be reported in the future. |
||[reStart](https://docs.byteplus.com/docs/DataFinder/Web_JS_SDK_API_Description#f89c147f) |Cancel the suspension of SDK reporting, usually after calling the disableSDK and planning to cancel the suspension, that is, restart the SDK reporting, and the reporting event will be resumed later. |
